H&P – Super Detailed

Consult Summary:
53-year-old male with 1-week history of non-painful, mildly warm swelling over the left olecranon; clinical impression olecranon bursitis. NSAID therapy initiated and blood tests arranged to rule out alternative inflammatory or infectious causes.

History:
• Chief complaint: “Weird swelling” on left elbow noticed ~1 week ago while showering.  
• Course: Stable over the week; no preceding trauma or repetitive strain; first occurrence.  
• Character: Visible fluctuant swelling; feels slightly warm; minimal tenderness just adjacent to the tip; full, pain-free range of motion.  
• No constitutional symptoms: denies fever, malaise, systemic illness.  
• No overlying erythema described; doctor noted dry skin at tip.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): no other joint swellings, no skin rash or eczema, no significant pain, no neurological deficit.  

Past Medical History:
• Osteoarthritis – GP-diagnosed “a few years ago”; joints occasionally painful.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.  

Allergies:
• Peanuts – food allergy (reaction details not discussed).  
• No known drug allergies.  

Medications:
• None on a regular basis.  
• New recommendation: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after food (OTC) – dose/route/frequency documented.  

Social History:
• Occupation: Desk job (non-manual).  
• Physical activity: Runs 2–3 times per week.  
• Tobacco: Not mentioned.  
• Alcohol / recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  

Family History:
• Denies known family history of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other rheumatologic disease. Further details not provided.

Physical Examination:
(Virtual video assessment)
• General: Well-appearing, mobile.  
• Left elbow: Localized swelling over olecranon bursa; skin dry; warmer than adjacent skin; minimal focal tenderness lateral to olecranon; full active movements maintained. No obvious erythema or surrounding cellulitis.  
• No other joint abnormalities visualized.  
• Vitals: Not obtained (video consult).

Investigations:
• Planned – phlebotomy form to be mailed:  
  – Inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR, CRP)  
  – Infection screen  
  – Rheumatologic antibody panel  
  – Uric acid / gout screen  
• No imaging ordered at this stage.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Suspected olecranon bursitis (left elbow)  
  • Assessment: Localized swelling, mild warmth, minimal pain, preserved function; no features suggesting septic arthritis currently.  
  • Plan:  
    – Start NSAID: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; discontinue if gastric irritation.  
    – Blood tests as above to exclude alternative inflammatory, infectious, or crystal arthropathies.  
    – Safety-net: If elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, spreads, or systemic symptoms develop, contact service urgently for same-day assessment to exclude septic arthritis.  
    – Follow-up: Arrange review (phone/video or in-person per patient preference) ~6 days after blood draw to assess clinical progress and review results.

Issue 2 – Background osteoarthritis  
  • Assessment: Historical diagnosis; currently asymptomatic except episodic joint pain.  
  • Plan: No change in management today; will reassess after bursitis evaluation if needed.

General plan items  
  • Education provided regarding nature of bursitis, expected course, and red-flag symptoms.  
  • Forms for blood work to be mailed; patient instructed on scheduling phlebotomy promptly.  
  • Encourage continuation of regular exercise within pain limits.

Quality checks:

• Missing but clinically expected: comprehensive medication list confirmation; vital signs; smoking and alcohol history; detailed allergy reaction description.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor filler words; no significant inaudible sections.
